explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a full-stack, multi-tenant AI-infra platform (“ACI.dev”) comprising:  
     • A React/Next.js frontend (“Dev Portal”)  
     • A FastAPI-based Python backend (Unified MCP server)  
     • A PostgreSQL database  
     • A CDK-driven AWS deployment layer  
     • 600+ external service connectors (apps/functions)  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level “frontend” folder: Next.js v13 app, Typescript, UI components, API-calling library  
   - Top-level “backend”: Python FastAPI monolith with Alembic migrations, CLI, routes, function executors, middleware, multi-tenant auth, rate-limit/quota, Sentry integration  
   - “apps” and “backend/apps”: JSON definitions for built-in integrations (app.json + functions.json)  
   - “backend/deployment”: AWS CDK stack provisioning VPC, ECS/EKS (or Lambda), RDS, KMS, IAM policies  
   - CI/CD: GitHub workflows under .github/workflows  

3. Key insights from README  
   - Purpose: expose 600+ tool integrations as unified function calls (MCP server) or via a lightweight Python SDK  
   - Multi-tenant authentication, dynamic discovery, natural-language permission boundaries  
   - Two primary access surfaces: Dev Portal (web UI) and Python SDK  

4. Main components & interactions (to include in your diagram)  
   A. Client Layer  
     1. Web Portal (Next.js)  
         – Hosts project settings, usage dashboards, interactive Playground  
         – Calls backend REST endpoints (HTTPS)  
     2. Python SDK  
         – Provides direct function-call API to same backend endpoints  
   B. API Layer / Unified MCP Server (FastAPI)  
     – Authentication & OAuth2 proxy  
     – Rate limiting & quota enforcement  
     – Route handlers for apps, functions, projects, analytics, linked-accounts, webhooks  
     – Function executor subsystem (base, REST, OAuth2, connector)  
     – CLI commands (create_agent, upsert_app, etc.)  
   C. Persistence & State  
     – PostgreSQL (SQLAlchemy + Alembic)  
     – KMS for encryption (secrets, API keys)  
   D. External Services  
     – 600+ third-party APIs via “app_connectors” (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, etc.)  
   E. Deployment / Infrastructure  
     – AWS VPC, ECS/EKS or Lambda, RDS, KMS, IAM (deployed via CDK)  
     – CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions)  

5. Relationships and data flows  
   - Browser/SDK → HTTPS → API Gateway/Load Balancer → FastAPI server  
   - FastAPI → SQL → PostgreSQL  
   - FastAPI → KMS → encrypted secrets  
   - FastAPI → External connectors → Third-party APIs  
   - CI/CD → Container registry → AWS (ECS/EKS) → running services  

6. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Plugin-style connector architecture: “app_connectors” directory for extensibility  
   - Layered architecture: Presentation (frontend), API (backend routes & executors), Data (DB & secrets)  
   - Multi-tenant isolation: per-project scoping in database and auth middleware  
   - Infrastructure as code: AWS CDK for repeatable provisioning  
   - Observability: Sentry integration for error tracking; GitHub Actions for CI  

7. Tailoring diagram elements  
   For this full-stack application:  
     • Distinct “Frontend” box (React/Next.js)  
     • “API Layer” box subdivided into Authentication, Rate-limit/Quota, Routes, Executors  
     • “Database” cylinder (PostgreSQL)  
     • “Secrets & Encryption” (AWS KMS)  
     • “Deployment” cluster (AWS CDK resources: ECS/EKS, RDS, IAM)  
     • “External Services” cloud icons (grouped or representative)  

8. Diagram construction guidelines  
   - Use rectangles for services/components (Frontend, API, CLI, CDK)  
   - Use a cylinder for the database  
   - Use cloud shapes for AWS infra and external APIs  
   - Draw directional arrows for request/response and data flows:  
       • Frontend → API → Database  
       • API → KMS → Database  
       • API → External Connectors → Third-party APIs  
       • CI/CD → Deployment resources  
   - Apply color-coding or varying shapes:  
       • Blue for internal components  
       • Green for infrastructure (AWS/CDK)  
       • Orange for external systems  
   - Label each arrow with protocol or data type (e.g., “HTTPS/JSON”, “SQL”, “KMS Encrypt/Decrypt”)  

9. Capture essential details without excessive clutter  
   - Group 600+ connectors under a single “App Connectors” sub-component, with a note “600+ JSON-driven integrations”  
   - Show both access methods (Web Portal and SDK) converging on the same API  
   - Highlight multi-tenant auth and dynamic function discovery in the API box  

By following these steps and using clear labels, directional arrows, and color-coded shapes, you’ll produce a comprehensive, accurate architecture diagram that communicates ACI.dev’s full-stack design, extensibility points, and deployment topology.  
</explanation>
